items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Listen to Kenny Clarke, you listen to Art Blakey. You know what I’m saying? You listen to Papa Jo Jones. You listen to Philly Joe Jones. These are the guys that I like, that I listen to

ctx.x: And tell us for instance how you go about trying to accomplish that legato nature on a drumset.

You listen to the masters. You duplicate your masters until you find it yourself, until you get it. And then you can be yourself. But everybody comes from somewhere. The history, you know you listen to the guys that originated the stuff. Listen to Kenny Clarke, you listen to Art Blakey. You know what I’m saying? You listen to Papa Jo Jones. You listen to Philly Joe Jones. These are the guys that I like, that I listen to, to see just how they emphasize a phrase, you see what I’m saying? And to see how they just…

same phrase — you might love him to death man, but you don’t want to play the same thing he played in the same places. It gets stale. Because jazz is not like that. I mean this, in the beginning when you were a kid and all the young guys wanted to play “Sing Sing Sing” like Gene Krupa. You know that was a show that you really listened to Gene and you’d say, “man I can play ‘Sing Sing Sing.’” But man you’ve got to get away from that. You’ve got to be yourself. You’ve got to learn how to express how you feel see…
